archetypes.name: code-robustness
archetypes.rationale: The new pattern allocates multiple temp files per fence and has conditional rm-f paths on every error branch; a resource-cleanup audit is needed to verify no leaks under partial-failure orderings, especially around the rc=3 special-case publish path.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every temp-file allocation in the three refactored SKILL.md fences (_route_stdout_file, _safe_route_env, _plan_review_stdout_file, _safe_step3_env, _publish_stdout_file, _safe_publish_env) for cleanup completeness: trace every early-exit branch to confirm the relevant rm -f calls are present. Pay special attention to the rc=3 publish path where _publish_input_is_temp is set true and a second temp file is created; verify that _publish_input is cleaned up on the read-result-env.sh failure branch and on the normal success path. Check whether set +e / set -e brackets around the read-result-env.sh calls are symmetric and whether a non-zero _rre_rc on the step3 path correctly preserves the temp file long enough for the stdout replay loop that follows. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: responsibility-boundary
archetypes.rationale: The diff moves argv-flag OR-merge responsibility from prompt-side SKILL.md orchestration into the design-route.sh driver; verifying the LLM boundary shift is complete and that no duplicate merge logic remains is an architectural concern not covered by the static correctness reviewer.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the prompt-side jq merge block for resume@* and already-planned routes has been fully removed from skills/design/SKILL.md Step 0b and that design-route.sh now owns this via merge_router_flags(). Check that SKILL.md passes all four argv flags (--partition-requested, --brainstorm-requested, --approve-requested, --skip-approve-requested) into the design-route.sh call so no flag is silently dropped. Confirm that the Brainstorm title-prefix auto-enable (BRAINSTORM_PREFIX=true → brainstorm_requested=true) in SKILL.md still fires after the route fence, not inside the driver where it could interact with the merge order. Inspect design-route.md Responsibility 4 to verify it accurately describes when merge_router_flags() fires relative to result-env write and WARN emission. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
